newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Afghan foes in rival claims on north town.
newsitem.headline: Afghan foes in rival claims on north town.

text.p: Afghanistan's Islamic Taleban government said on Wednesday its forces had captured the northeastern town of Taloqan, headquarters of ousted President Burhanuddin Rabbani, from opposition forces.
But an opposition spokesman denied that Taloqan, capital of Takhar province, had fallen to the Taleban militia.
There was no independent confirmation of either report.
"The Taleban today captured Taloqan in fighting in which tens of (opposition) militiamen were killed and hundreds were captured," the official Kabul radio said.

The broadcast followed a report by a private Afghan news service based in neighbouring Pakistan that said the Taleban had captured Taloqan with the support of local commanders and people after an overnight offensive from the neighbouring Kunduz province.
Opposition spokesman Dr Abdullah told reporters in Kabul by talephone that the Taleban were nowhere near Taloqan.
"Taleban forces are neither in Taloqan nor anywhere else in Takhar province," he said.

He acknowledged that Taleban supporters had entered the Bangi area of Takhar from Kunduz on Tuesday but said they were driven out on Wednesday by the forces of former government military commander Ahmad Shah Masood.

Abdullah, speaking by telephone from the opposition-held Panjsher Valley north of Kabul, said Masood's forces had crushed a revolt by a local Pashtun tribe in Takhar and also taken Chardara district in central Kunduz, killing 150 pro-Taleban fighters.
But the Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) service quoted unspecified Afghan opposition sources in the Pakistani border town of Peshawar as confirming the fall of Taloqan.
Rabbani and Abdurrab Rasul Sayyaf, chief of the Ittehad-i-Islami faction, have used Taloqan as a base since the Taleban drove the Rabbani government from Kabul in September.

AIP said the Taleban, who control more than two-thirds of Afghanistan, had launched a major offensive into Takhar province from Kunduz on Tuesday evening, killing 20 soldiers loyal to Masood and capturing 285 after intense fighting. It said the Taleban had lost eight soldiers.
AIP said two helicopters had taken off from Taloqan for an undisclosed destination on Tuesday, apparently with opposition leaders on board, but it did not identify them.
Abdullah said Rabbani had been in the main northern opposition-held town of Mazar-i-Sharif for the past few days.
